description: Drawings, RFIs, submittals, daily logs, inspections, and punch lists at about 140 jobsites
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: About 28,600 workers on site each day depend on current drawings and RFI answers; building from a superseded drawing is a quality and safety risk; offline tablet caches last about one shift
manual_workaround: Offline drawing sync on tablets; printed current sets in each trailer; paper RFI and daily log forms entered later
dependent_third_parties: Project management platform vendor; cellular carriers
quantified_impact_basis: About 15% productivity loss on self-perform labor (about $2.1 million) plus general conditions and schedule delay exposure (about $2.5 million) per day
acquired_business_dependency: AQ-1 projects use the same platform
single_points_of_failure: Single project management platform (SaaS) for all projects

description: Monthly pay apps with schedules of values, lien waivers, and certified payroll attachments; federal invoices through government portals
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: About 300 pay apps worth about $400 million a month are submitted from the 20th to the 25th; a missed window defers cash by a month for many owners; federal invoices follow prompt payment rules
manual_workaround: Pay apps prepared from the ERP and sent through owner portals or by courier; federal invoices entered manually in government portals
dependent_third_parties: ERP hosting (Cloud provider A); e-signature service; owner portals; federal invoicing portals
dependent_people_or_facilities: Project managers; project accountants; billing team
quantified_impact_basis: Collections deferred (not lost): about $13.2 million of owner receipts per day; carrying cost of about $15,000 per day at the revolver rate
acquired_business_dependency: AQ-1 bills from its own ERP (see BP-17)
single_points_of_failure: None (ERP has a warm standby region)

description: Accounts payable runs twice a week: about 10,500 ACH payments a month to about 7,500 payees (about $300 million)
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Subcontractors stop work or file liens when paid late; FAR 52.232-27(c)(1) requires payment within 7 days of receiving a federal payment; state prompt payment laws add interest
manual_workaround: Manual ACH file built in the bank portal for critical payees, with dual approval; checks for small payees
dependent_third_parties: Three treasury banks; bank account validation service
quantified_impact_basis: Late payment interest, work stoppages, and lien handling on about $35 million per payment run
acquired_business_dependency: AQ-1 payment files enter the payment hub from the AQ-1 ERP
single_points_of_failure: Single payment file transfer gateway cluster

description: Payment Operations verifies every new payee and every bank-account change by call-back to a known number and the bank account validation service before the change is released
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Changed payees can be held without harm for about 2 days; the change log must be exact because it is the evidence for insurance claims and recalls
manual_workaround: Hold all payments to changed accounts; manual call-back log on paper; release only after second-person review
quantified_impact_basis: About $1.5 million of payments to changed accounts held per day; fraud exposure if the control fails is one diverted payment of up to about $5 million
acquired_business_dependency: AQ-1 vendor master changes are made in the AQ-1 ERP without Payment Operations review (gap)
single_points_of_failure: Bank account validation service (no fallback other than call-back)

description: Daily cash positioning, wires, positive pay decisions, and covenant reporting
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Positive pay decisions are due the same day; payroll and tax funding wires have fixed cut-off times
manual_workaround: Bank portals used directly with dual approval; phone instructions to relationship managers using pre-agreed codes
quantified_impact_basis: Missed wire cut-offs, overdraft and penalty costs, and returned positive pay items

description: Weekly craft payroll for about 6,600 workers, salaried payroll, and weekly certified payrolls on about 120 federal and prevailing wage jobs
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Craft workers are paid weekly; late wages trigger wage law penalties and walk-offs; certified payrolls are due weekly on federal jobs (FAR 52.222-8)
manual_workaround: Repeat the prior week's payroll with adjustments; off-cycle checks; certified payroll forms prepared from timesheets
quantified_impact_basis: About $11 million weekly craft payroll at risk of delay; penalty, overtime, and productivity loss
acquired_business_dependency: AQ-1 uses the same payroll vendor

description: Quantity takeoff, pricing, subcontractor bid leveling, and bid submission (about $1 billion of bids a month)
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Bid due times are fixed and late bids are rejected; on bid day the effective MTD is 4 hours
manual_workaround: Bid templates on encrypted laptops; phone and fax bids from subcontractors; hand delivery
dependent_third_parties: Estimating software vendor; AI bid assistant vendor; owner and federal bid portals
quantified_impact_basis: Expected margin on a missed bid (about $28 million average bid at about 7% margin)

description: Design-build and MILCON work with CUI drawings in the FPCE and controlled plan rooms at 16 installation jobsites
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Installation jobsites cannot use commercial systems for CUI; DoD contracts carry liquidated damages; CUI must stay in assessed systems (DFARS 252.204-7012; 252.204-7021)
manual_workaround: Printed CUI drawing sets in plan rooms; enclave access from HQ-1 if a site link fails
dependent_third_parties: Government community cloud provider; cellular carriers
dependent_people_or_facilities: 16 federal project security managers; Federal Group project teams
quantified_impact_basis: Schedule delay and liquidated damages exposure on 16 installation jobsites (about $640 million a year of DoD work)
acquired_business_dependency: AQ-2 DoD projects hold FCI only

description: Model coordination, clash detection, and shop drawing review on GPU virtual desktops
process_owner: Vice President, Virtual Design and Construction
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Coordination meetings can slip two days without schedule impact on most projects
manual_workaround: Local model copies on workstations; design team models reviewed in vendor viewers
dependent_systems: SYS-07 (Cloud provider A virtual desktops); SYS-01
dependent_third_parties: Cloud provider A; BIM software vendors
quantified_impact_basis: Coordination delays and rework on active projects

description: Prequalification, buyout, subcontract execution, flowdowns, insurance and bond compliance
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Buyout schedules have slack of several days; flowdowns must precede subcontract award
manual_workaround: Paper subcontracts from templates; email-free courier signatures
quantified_impact_basis: Delayed buyout and starts on new projects

description: 24x7 remote monitoring and administration of client access control, video, and building automation systems in about 420 buildings
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Service contracts commit to 2-hour restoration; clients rely on BTS alerts for door forced and camera offline events
manual_workaround: Client on-site staff take over local monitoring consoles; BTS technicians dispatched to priority sites
dependent_third_parties: Cloud provider B; remote access gateway vendor
quantified_impact_basis: Service level credits and emergency dispatch costs; client safety impact dominates

description: Owner-facing budgets, pay app review, change orders, schedules, and document control for about 35 institutional owners
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Owner boards and pay app approvals run on monthly cycles; contracts commit to 12-hour restoration
manual_workaround: Exports emailed to owners through the secure file-transfer portal
quantified_impact_basis: Service credits and owner approval delays

description: Pre-task plans, inspections, incident reporting, and OSHA recordkeeping
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Serious incidents must be reported promptly and pre-task plans are required before work starts each day
manual_workaround: Paper pre-task plans and incident forms; phone reporting to the safety hotline
quantified_impact_basis: Delayed starts and documentation rework; safety impact dominates

description: Equipment dispatch, telematics, maintenance, and prefabrication scheduling at YD-1 and YD-2
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Equipment moves are planned a week ahead

description: Monthly close, quarterly and annual SEC reports, and SOX controls
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Monthly close tolerates 5 days; in the quarter-end window the MTD drops to 48 hours because of SEC filing deadlines
manual_workaround: Close from last ERP extracts and bank statements
acquired_business_dependency: AQ-1 consolidates from its own ERP

business_process: Jobsite access control and time capture
description: Badging and gate access for about 28,600 daily workers; time clocks feeding payroll
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Installation gates need badge lists daily; time data feeds weekly payroll
manual_workaround: Paper sign-in sheets and printed badge lists; manual time cards
quantified_impact_basis: Gate delays and manual time entry

business_process: AQ-1 project accounting, billing, and AP
description: AQ-1 billing, accounts payable, and vendor master in the AQ-1 legacy ERP until migration (due 2027-03-31)
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: AQ-1 is about 6% of revenue; its billing follows the same monthly window
manual_workaround: Manual pay apps from spreadsheets; AP through the enterprise payment hub with Payment Operations verification
dependent_systems: AQ-1 legacy ERP (on-premises, Texas); AQ-1 email tenant; SYS-06
quantified_impact_basis: About $0.77 million of AQ-1 revenue per day deferred plus rework
single_points_of_failure: AQ-1 legacy ERP server (nightly backup only)
